proposed_widenings.name: ProficiencyGrantSubject.saving_throw
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature grants proficiency in all saving throws. ProficiencyGrantSubject covers skill / weapon_category / armor_category but has no saving_throw variant. This is the canonical D&D mechanic of adding PB to a save; it needs a dedicated subject kind.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws.

proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_reroll
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature lets the monk reroll a failed saving throw and keep the new result. modify_roll_reroll exists in the v4 taxonomy (Section 9, effect atoms) but is absent from types.ts. No existing atom covers forced rerolls of an already-resolved d20 test.
proposed_widenings.evidence: whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll

proposed_widenings.name: ReactionTrigger.any_failed_saving_throw
proposed_widenings.justification: The activation trigger is 'whenever you make a saving throw and fail'. The existing spell_save_outcome trigger is scoped to saving throws caused by spells. A general any_failed_saving_throw variant (not spell-scoped) is needed for class feature reactions.
proposed_widenings.evidence: whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it

proposed_widenings.name: shared_class_resource_reference
proposed_widenings.justification: Focus Points are a Monk class-level shared pool established at Level 2 (Monk Discipline Points / Focus Points). Multiple Monk features draw from this single pool. The current surface models each activated feature as owning its own resource; there is no mechanism to express 'expend from the character's existing Focus Point pool' without declaring a new independent resource per feature, which would be dishonest.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it

notes: The unit naturally decomposes into a CompositeClassFeatureMechanics with two parts: (1) a PassiveMechanics granting saving throw proficiency in all six abilities, and (2) an ActivatedAbilityMechanics triggered by any failed save that spends a Focus Point to reroll. Both parts hit surface gaps. Gap 1 (saving throw proficiency subject) blocks the passive part. Gaps 2-4 block the activation part. The composite family itself exists and would be the right shape. The Focus Point shared-resource issue is the deepest gap — it exposes that the surface currently cannot express 'reference this character's existing class resource pool' without per-feature resource duplication. No dhall/json/trace authored: encoding would require lying about at least three surface shapes.
